newsitem.title: USA: Bergen Brunswig reports flat earnings; charge from failed merger.
newsitem.headline: Bergen Brunswig reports flat earnings; charge from failed merger.

text.p: Bergen Brunswig Corp., the maker of pharmaceuticals and medical-surgical products, Tuesday reported flat earnings for the latest quarter, which included a charge of nearly $3.5 million for the company's decision last month to call off its $1.6 billion merger with IVAX Corp.
The company said it earned $20.5 million, or 51 cents a share, in its fiscal second quarter, which ended on March 31, vs. year earlier earnings of $20.4 million, or 51 cents.
It reported revenues of $2.89 billion, up from $2.45 billion.
Bergen said its results included a charge of $3.4 million related to its unsuccessful merger with IVAX, a Miami-based generic drug maker.
It said that, excluding the merger expenses, earnings rose 17 percent to $23.9 million, equual to 59 cents a share.

On March 20 Bergen terminated the merger talks and announced that it was suing IVAX, alleging "breaches" in the agreement. Later, IVAX launched a lawsuit of its own against Bergen, also charging it with breach of agreement.
In its earnings report Tuesday, Bergen said it would seek to recover its merger expenses of $5.8 million from the failed IVAX deal.
Bergen's stock was up 12.5 cents at $30.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
